open_points.subject: staff_session_ttl_hours configuration status
open_points.text: A30 calls the listed values “Runtime knobs with confirmed defaults” and says “its value is configuration,” while the changed passage says “the staff session lifetime is fixed in source”; the State 2 Status also says the confirmed config defaults “remain runtime knobs.”
open_points.question: Is the 12-hour staff session lifetime an environment-configurable runtime value or an immutable source constant, and if it is immutable, what happens when a deployment supplies a corresponding environment variable?
options: The environment may override the 12-hour default.
The value is always 12 hours and a supplied override is ignored.
The value is always 12 hours and a supplied override makes startup fail.
open_points.default_guess: Treat 12 hours as fixed in source and reject a recognized attempted override at startup.

witness.initial: The service source fixes staff sessions at 12 hours; the deployment environment contains STAFF_SESSION_TTL_HOURS=1.
events: The host operator starts the service.
A staff member logs in successfully.
outcomes: The environment value is treated as a runtime-knob override, so the session expires after 1 hour.
The source constant controls, so the session remains valid for 12 hours; the supplied value is ignored or rejected at startup.
witness.observer: The host operator and the logged-in staff member.

open_points.subject: environment-variable override surface for runtime knobs
open_points.text: The changed passage says “a deployment changes only the values it supplies through the environment,” but the table names environment variables only for registry_endpoint_env_name, email_gateway_url_env_name, and binary_read_limit_env_name; it gives no environment names or supplied-value behavior for registry_timeout_seconds, email_gateway_timeout_seconds, viewer_session_ttl_days, challenge TTLs, the challenge rate limit, or credential entropy.
open_points.question: Exactly which listed knobs are environment-configurable, under what environment-variable names, and are unknown or attempted non-configurable settings ignored or startup errors?
options: Only entries with an explicit *_env_name are read from the environment.
Every listed runtime knob except the source-fixed staff lifetime has an environment variable whose name must be specified.
The later config.runtime_environment_variables table determines the allowlist, but its complete contents must be stated here for State 2 consumers.
open_points.default_guess: Allow environment overrides only for explicitly named environment variables and keep every other listed value at its stated default.

witness.initial: A deployment supplies REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30; no explicitly named environment variable for registry_timeout_seconds appears in the accepted texts.
events: The host operator starts the service.
The portal makes a Registry request that has not answered after 5 seconds.
outcomes: The service recognizes the supplied runtime-knob override and continues waiting up to 30 seconds.

The service recognizes only explicitly named environment variables and fails the Registry request at the 5-second default; another implementation may instead reject the environment setting at startup.
witness.observer: The API caller and the host operator.
